title: Equimultiple weak transforms: order bound and exceptional nondivisibility
statement: Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary transverse to $N$ (its local equations restrict to distinct coordinate parameters on $N$). Let $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent and $d\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q\ge0:I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with value $\infty$ for zero, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge d\}$. A test transformation is an open restriction, a smooth-center blowup in cosupport with normal crossings with $E$, a product with a line adjoining its zero section to $E$, or a blowup of the intersection of two boundary hypersurfaces. For a cosupport blowup use the strict transform of $N$ and the ideal $e^{-d}\sigma^*I$, where $e$ is the exceptional equation; for the last two operations use ordinary pullback. Assume $I$ is nonzero on every component, $\operatorname{ord}_x I\le d$ everywhere, and the smooth center $T\subseteq\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)$ has normal crossings with $E$. For its blowup $\sigma$, the weak transform $I^{\mathrm w}=e^{-d}\sigma^*I$ is coherent, has order at most $d$ at every point, and is not divisible by the ideal of any component of the new exceptional divisor. If $I$ has no factor from any component of $E$, then $I^{\mathrm w}$ has no factor from any surviving strict transform of those components either. More explicitly, in coordinates $(u_1,\ldots,u_r,w)$ with $T=V(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, each generator has expansion $f=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge d}f_\alpha(w)u^\alpha$ in the completion along $T$; in the $i$-chart its weak transform is $\sum f_\alpha(w)e^{|\alpha|-d}(u/e)^\alpha$. At every point of $T$ some degree-$d$ coefficient of some generator is a unit. The degree-$d$ polynomial on the normal fibre is nonzero, and its dehomogenization has degree at most $d$. The assertions commute with smooth pullback. proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] with $J=I$, $c=d$, and $C=T$. Its hypotheses are exactly the smooth pair, the normal crossings condition, and the inclusion of the center in cosupport. It gives $I\subseteq P^d$, where $P=\mathcal I_{T,N}$, the identification $N'=\operatorname{Bl}_T N$, smooth coordinate charts, and a regular coherent ideal $I^{\mathrm w}=e^{-d}\sigma^*I$. It also gives the unchanged complement, the new normal crossings boundary, and smooth-base-change compatibility of these constructions. No component of $N$ can lie in $T$: at its generic point the nonzero ideal is the unit ideal and has order zero. Thus the charts used below cover all of $N'$. The empty center requires no exceptional calculation.

proof.text: Work locally in one of those coordinate charts, with coordinates $(w,u)$ and $T=V(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$. The formal completion along $T$ is $\mathcal O_T[[u_1,\ldots,u_r]]$, locally on $T$. Here is the identification, including its coefficients. Both this chart and $T\times\mathbf A^r$ are etale over the coordinate affine space and are identified on $u=0$. An etale map is flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] extends this identification uniquely across each successive square-zero thickening $(u)^{n+1}/(u)^{n+2}$. The thickening kernel squares to zero since $2(n+1)\ge n+2$ for $n\ge0$; choose affine coordinate neighbourhoods throughout, as required by the cited lifting statement. Apply the lifting statement in both directions; uniqueness makes their composites identities and makes the lifts compatible as $n$ increases. Taking the inverse limit gives the claimed identification. Consequently every local generator has a unique expansion $f=\sum_\alpha f_\alpha(w)u^\alpha$, with coefficients regular on $T$. Since $I\subseteq P^d$ by Step 1, all coefficients with $|\alpha|<d$ vanish. This is an expansion in the formal completion, not a claim that the series converges in the original coordinate ring.

source.place: Tag 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale), with Definition 02HG (definition-formally-etale); agent construction of compatible coordinate thickenings after Tag 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure).

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$. If every coefficient $f_\alpha(t)$ with $|\alpha|=d$ were zero for every generator, the expansion modulo $P^{d+1}$ would express each generator as a sum of degree-$d$ monomials in the $u_j$ with coefficients in $\mathfrak m_t$, plus an element of $P_t^{d+1}$. This is an identity in the actual finite quotient $\mathcal O_{N,t}/P_t^{d+1}$, supplied by the compatible thickening isomorphisms of Step 2. Lift the finitely many degree-$d$ coefficients to $\mathcal O_{N,t}$; coefficients vanishing in $\kappa(t)$ lift into $\mathfrak m_t$, and the discrepancy is in $P_t^{d+1}$. Thus $I_t\subseteq\mathfrak m_t^{d+1}$, contradicting $\operatorname{ord}_t I\le d$. Hence one degree-$d$ coefficient is a unit in $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Equivalently some generator has a nonzero homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomial $H_t(U)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}f_\alpha(t)U^\alpha$ over $\kappa(t)$. This argument uses stalks and therefore includes nonclosed points.

proof.text: Let $y\in N'$ lie over $t\in T$, in an $i$-chart. Apply [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus] with $B$ this smooth chart, empty $h$-family ($r=0$ in that lemma), and all chart coordinates in its $w$-list. Its centered local Taylor map is therefore available at $y$, with residue field $L=\kappa(y)$. This local map is continuous for maximal-ideal powers: it sends every product of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak m_y$ to the $n$-th power of the Taylor maximal ideal. Hence the finite-jet identity of Step 4 remains valid after Taylor expansion. Set its exceptional variable to zero and its base-coordinate increments to zero. The Taylor series of the transformed generator from Step 4 then becomes the polynomial $Q_t(v(y)+V)$ in the ratio-coordinate increments. Extension $\kappa(t)\to L$ is injective and translation is an invertible polynomial substitution, so this polynomial is nonzero and has degree at most $d$. Some Taylor term of total degree at most $d$ therefore survives. Since a local homomorphism to the Taylor ring sends $\mathfrak m_y^{d+1}$ into the power-series maximal ideal to power $d+1$, the generator is not in $\mathfrak m_y^{d+1}$. Hence $\operatorname{ord}_y I^{\mathrm w}\le d$. The same nonzero polynomial shows that this generator is not divisible by $e$ in $\mathcal O_{N',y}$: divisibility would force its Taylor series to vanish after setting the exceptional variable to zero. Thus the ideal has no new exceptional component as a factor, even locally at any point of that divisor. Outside the exceptional divisor the blowup is an isomorphism by Step 1, so the original order bound applies.

source.place: Agent Taylor calculation in the smooth coordinate charts of Tags 0FUE and 0FUT; the cited Taylor lemma provides the regular centered Taylor map at arbitrary points.

proof.text: Work locally on $N$ and let $D$ be an integral component of its induced old boundary with nonempty strict transform $D'$. The integral-component convention is [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]; a restricted ambient component may have several such branches, which are treated separately. The generic point of $D'$ lies in the inverse image of $D\setminus T$, and there the chart identification of Step 1 gives the original ideal, multiplied only by a unit. Since $I$ has no $D$ factor, its restriction to the integral scheme $D$ is nonzero at the generic point; the same is true for $I^{\mathrm w}$ on $D'$. Therefore $I^{\mathrm w}$ is not contained in $\mathcal I_{D'}$. Explicitly, divisibility by the prime local equation of an integral Cartier divisor is detected at its generic point: if a local element lies in $(h)A_{(h)}$, then $sf\in(h)$ for some $s\notin(h)$, and primality gives $f\in(h)$. This also shows that no local boundary factor has appeared. Components whose strict transform is empty require no assertion.

source.place: Agent generic-point calculation for integral boundary Cartier divisors; blowup complement from Step 1.

proof.text: Finally, the geometric charts and the controlled-transform ideal commute with smooth pullback by [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts]. The statement “Orders and $D_E^j$ commute with smooth pullback” in [lem-trf-logarithmic-differential-transform] gives equality of point orders at every point above a given point, including changes of relative dimension. Hence the hypotheses and the order bound persist. The formulas in Step 4 pull back coefficient by coefficient. On every new normal fibre the nonzero degree-$d$ form remains nonzero after the residue-field extension, so Steps 4--5 still exclude exceptional factors. For an old boundary branch $D$, apply that same order equality to the image ideal in $\mathcal O_D$ and the induced smooth map on boundary schemes. This ideal is nonzero in every stalk when there is no boundary factor. Its finite orders stay finite after pullback, so its pullback image cannot be zero; hence no old boundary factor appears. The coordinate boundary equations also pull back to the corresponding coordinate boundary. This proves all the claimed smooth compatibility.
